note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  New-onset left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia x ~1 day; fluctuates but persistent; improved lying down; not worse with bending forward or cough/sneeze; no nausea/vomiting; no fever measured; no focal neurologic symptoms. No known chronic conditions documented.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother with hypertension and migraines.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive); dose/route/frequency not documented. Paracetamol (acetaminophen) taken for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented. Reports aspirin “allergy” (causes nausea). Prior use of NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen/naproxen) tolerated historically; not taken in last few days.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  On combined oral contraceptive (Microgynon). Last menstrual period ~1 week ago. No headache relationship to menstrual cycle reported.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Eating and drinking okay. Tobacco: denies. Alcohol: a few drinks on weekends. Illicit drugs: denies. Recent work-related stress.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Denies visual changes; photophobia present. Hearing concerns not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Work stress noted; no mood symptoms or self-harm risk recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Lives with housemates; confidential setting for telehealth confirmed. Other social factors not recorded.  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (teleconsultation). Patient has no thermometer at home; no current BP reading; BP reportedly normal ~6 months ago.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of findings: Acute, first-episode unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia in a woman using a combined oral contraceptive. No fever, meningismus, visual changes, nausea/vomiting, or focal neurologic deficits. Headache improves in the dark and with rest; better lying down. Family history of migraine and hypertension.  
- Relevant differentials (consistent with DDx and transcript):  
  - Migraine without aura (first episode): Features of unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, moderate–severe intensity, rest preference; family history supportive.  
  - Tension-type headache: Possible with recent stress, though phenotype (unilateral, throbbing, photophobia) is less typical.  
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): Consider due to estrogen-containing OCP and new significant headache; currently no neurologic deficits or progressive features.  
  - Lower-likelihood considerations: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (no thunderclap or neuro signs), viral meningitis (no fever/neck stiffness).  
- Working diagnosis: Probable migraine without aura (first episode).  
- Plan:  
  - Trial NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) in addition to paracetamol/acetaminophen as advised; maintain hydration; rest in dark room.  
  - Safety-net: Seek urgent care if worsening headache, new neurologic symptoms, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or change in character.  
  - Arrange BP check (has not been checked recently at home; last clinic check ~6 months ago reportedly normal).  
  - Obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature during illness.  
  - If headaches persist, recur, or show cycle-related pattern, schedule follow-up for further assessment and preventive options; consider evaluation to exclude secondary causes (including CVST) if red flags or atypical course emerge.  
- Conflicts: None between transcript and DDx noted.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed hydration and appropriate analgesic use; advised monitoring for red flags and seeking prompt review if they occur.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Not recorded.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Advised to arrange BP check soon. Follow-up if headache not settling in 1–2 days or if recurrent/cyclical. Immediate contact if red flags develop.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine without aura (High): Unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, moderate–severe intensity, rest preference; family history of migraine; no neurologic deficits.  
- Tension-type headache (Medium): Recent work stress and lack of neurologic/systemic features; phenotype less typical due to unilateral throbbing and photophobia.  
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Medium): Estrogen-containing OCP is a risk; new significant headache; absence of focal deficits lowers immediate concern but warrants vigilance.

- Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals (BP, pulse), temperature, anthropometrics, neurologic exam, or urinalysis; no immunization review; no chronic disease screening (lipids/glucose), cancer screening (cervical, breast, bowel), or bone health assessment documented.
